subject: Production: 5xx/429 spike — GPU capacity depletion affecting Starlight inference
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <cnguyen@starlight.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@starlight.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production: API 5xx spike impacting inference for Starlight - urgent

Markus / Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoint (starlight-main:production) at ~08:05 UTC. Client requests are timing out (~10s) and retrying — our side is observing request fanouts and user-facing errors. This is affecting nightly batch jobs and some customer-facing features.

Attached are a short log dump and the service metrics around the window. Can you confirm you're seeing the same and what immediate mitigations you can apply? This is causing revenue-impacting errors for some customers.

Thanks,
Claire
Ops Lead
Starlight AI

Attachments: stack-trace-log-20270211.txt (text), svc-metrics-08-12-2027.csv (csv)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <cnguyen@starlight.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: API 5xx spike impacting inference for Starlight - urgent

Claire — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. We’re seeing matching error-rate and timeout spikes on our dashboards (5xx and 429s concentrated on the hosted pool serving your account). I’ve looped in Lauren (ops) and Rishi (runtime) to triage.

Initial notes / ask:
- Could you confirm the predominant request pattern (average sequence length, batching behavior) for the failing calls?
- Any recent change on your side (traffic spike, rollout)?

Immediate actions I’m requesting from infra: bump pool capacity and enable our faster fallback routing to a compatible, smaller-parameter model to reduce memory footprint. Will update with timeline in the next 10–15m.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:29:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: API 5xx spike impacting inference for Starlight - urgent

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 08:22 GMT, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Claire — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. We’re seeing matching error-rate and timeout spikes on our dashboards (5xx and 429s concentrated on the hosted pool serving your account). I’ve looped in Lauren (ops) and Rishi (runtime) to triage.

Confirmed: telemetry shows sustained GPU memory pressure and a backlog of pending requests in the hosted pool assigned to Starlight. Root cause hypothesis: sudden traffic with long contexts + a few large batches pushed node memory above reservation, triggering OOMs on some driver instances and causing retries to amplify. The autoscaler is healthy but configured with a conservative cooldown (300s) and scale-step limits; that caused a multi-minute gap before new instances joined the pool.

Short-term mitigation (executed / immediate):
- Increase target replica count by +30% for the affected hosted pool (applied at 08:27 UTC).
- Apply temporary routing override to route requests matching Starlight's API key to model variant "rwd-compact-v1" (lower memory, slightly lower context ceiling) at 08:32 UTC.
- Throttle max batch size at ingress for Starlight to avoid big fused allocations.

Notes: these reduce the pressure but are not permanent fixes. Post-incident: we should tune autoscaler cooldown, add pre-warm policy for accounts with bursty nightly jobs, and add a safety throttle on client-side retries.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: API 5xx spike impacting inference for Starlight - urgent

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 08:29 GMT, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Confirmed: telemetry shows sustained GPU memory pressure and a backlog of pending requests in the hosted pool assigned to Starlight.

Action log (what I ran):
- 08:27 UTC: scaled hosted-pool-starlight from 20 -> 26 replicas (aws/g4dn cluster).
- 08:31 UTC: enabled routing override to rwd-compact-v1 for Starlight API key.
- 08:33 UTC: set ingress max_batch_size=8 for Starlight temporarily.
- 08:36 UTC: observed error-rate drop from 18% -> 4% and 429s falling by ~70%.

Next steps:
- Keep routes in fallback for 2 hours while we monitor.
- Run a short cleanup and repro: collect KV-cache sizes and exact OOM traces (attached).
- Schedule follow-up postmortem and include account team to discuss customer-facing remedies.

Attaching runbook actions we performed.

— Hannah
Head of Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-actions-20270211.md
From: Claire Nguyen <cnguyen@starlight.ai>

Thanks — we can confirm the drop in errors saw user traffic recover. Tough impact window: a set of customer-facing workflows failed between 08:05–08:35 UTC and we saw increased support tickets.

Two asks:
1) We need an ETA for white-glove remediation (postmortem and corrective timeline).
2) Starlight will request a goodwill credit for the impacted usage window and would like an exec-to-exec contact to discuss contractual impact.

Please put us in touch with someone in leadership who can speak to credits and next steps.

— Claire
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Exec summary: Starlight production 5xx/429 spike (GPU capacity + autoscale lag) — request for credit approval

Marissa — quick summary for your executive review and approval:

Impact:
- Customer: Starlight AI (HubSpot deal SLIGHT-4231).
- Incident window: ~08:05–08:35 UTC (error rates peaked at ~18% 5xx/429).
- Business impact: customer-visible failures for batch and interactive flows; support tickets opened.

What happened (short):
- A burst of traffic with long sequences and larger-than-typical batch sizes drove memory pressure on their assigned hosted GPU pool. Several driver instances experienced OOM-related failures; retries amplified requests while autoscaler cooldown delayed additional capacity.

Actions taken:
- Scaled pool +30% at 08:27 UTC.
- Enabled routing to compact model variant at 08:32 UTC.
- Throttled ingress batch size to reduce fused allocations.

Customer asks:
- Postmortem with timeline and corrective actions.
- Goodwill credit for impacted consumption window.
- Exec-level contact for contractual discussion.

Recommendation: approve a one-time credit equivalent to 2x the impacted usage for the window as a gesture of goodwill and assign an AE/Director to lead the customer touchpoint. I propose I join the call with Claire and your sales lead.

Please advise and I’ll set up the call.

— Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
